comparison: Perfect agreement on CDR3 coverage and accuracy claims (C17, C18, C46). Both evaluations find the data well-supported, with OpenEval noting the mechanistic inference is reasonable but speculative, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings through their overall positive assessment.

Complete agreement on the negative finding regarding global resolution correlation (C19, C47). Both evaluations accept the observation and mechanistic explanation, with OpenEval suggesting local resolution analysis would strengthen conclusions, while peer reviewers do not challenge the interpretation.

Disagreement on confidence level for EMPEM application (C28-C31, C33). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of ground truth validation and reliance on extrapolation from benchmark, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly acknowledging the ~17% success rate with appropriate qualification.

Agreement on comparative advantages of cryoEM over proteomics (C34-C36). Both evaluations find these claims supported, with OpenEval noting they are based on established field knowledge rather than new data, and peer reviewers implicitly accepting through positive assessment.

Disagreement on current limitations (C37, C38). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative statements without quantitative support, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the transparent discussion of limitations as consistent with measured evaluation. Peer R8 also includes C50 which OpenEval addresses in R2.

Agreement on background mixing experiments and integration approach (C26-C27, C32, C48-C49, C54-C55). Both find these well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes systematic experimental design, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the integration approach and improved accuracy with templates. Peer R5 also covers CR3022 proof-of-principle (C20-C25) which OpenEval addresses separately in R5.

Agreement on methodological modifications (C41-C43). Both evaluations find these supported, with OpenEval noting implementation is straightforward but validation of weighting scheme not explicit, while peer reviewers affirm the methodological approach as 'appropriate and fair.' Peer R9 also includes benchmark construction claims (C39-C40, C44) which OpenEval addresses in R1.

Partial overlap on benchmark assembly and methodology (C8-C10). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R1 focuses on benchmark assembly methodology (C8-C10, C39-C40, C44), while peer R1 emphasizes core workflow validation findings (C8-C10, C13-C16, C45, C51), with explicit reviewer affirmation that 'tests constructed seem appropriate and fair.'

Substantial overlap on benchmark analysis results (C13-C16, C45, C51). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R2 provides detailed statistical validation (Kolmogorov-Smirnov, p<0.0001) for correlation findings (C12-C16, C45, C50-C53), while peer R1 affirms the workflow works 'pretty well' and evidence is 'solid,' covering subset of these claims.

Agreement on error rates and V-gene assignment (C12, C52). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation with appropriate statistical testing, while peer reviewers implicitly accept that despite higher error rates, V-gene assignment remains possible, not challenging the finding or interpretation.

Agreement on CR3022 proof-of-principle experiment (C20-C25). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes well-controlled experiment with clear quantification and known MS limitations, while peer R5 also encompasses broader integration approach validation (C26-C27, C32, C48-C49, C54-C55) which OpenEval addresses separately in R6.

Overlap on benchmark construction methodology (C39-C40, C44). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R1 emphasizes explicit methodology description with internal consistency, while peer R9 affirms methodological approach and benchmark construction through positive assessment of results, also covering software modifications (C41-C43).

Minimal overlap on alignment score interpretation (C50). OpenEval R2 rates benchmark analysis as SUPPORTED with detailed statistical validation, while peer R8 addresses current limitations and quality-dependent nature, rating as SUPPORTED the transparent discussion of constraints including alignment score thresholds.
